reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is right. Five WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $650 for exactly this visit establish price and demand; LumenTech Field Service is the recorded fulfiller with a written quote ($300/visit), stated capacity (all five in the first 14 days) and net-15 terms, and is the plan's delivery performer. 5 x $650 = $3,250 settles by day 24 (visit by day 14 + pay within 10), above the $3,000 settled-cash target inside 30 days. For any visit day v the cinema pays by v+10 and LumenTech is due v+15, so the supplier is always paid from receipts and no owner capital is advanced; net after LumenTech is $1,750.
findings: Recomputed: 5 x $650 = $3,250 by day 24; supplier 5 x $300 = $1,500 due by day 29; net $1,750; cash never negative; proof day 24 < 30.
The target is gross settled cash (metric SETTLED_CASH), which $3,250 meets; the owner should understand $1,500 of it is owed to LumenTech by day 29.

Margin is one deal: if one cinema does not pay, $2,600 < $3,000. The $240 workbook backup does not cover that shortfall as evidenced - its price is comparable listings on the alliance store (other sellers' asks), not a purchase price - so it is a test, not a reserve.
Card humanHours 0.5 per deal is not shown in the plan; no owner-hours limit applies.
Executor SEND_A_MESSAGE / ISSUE_AN_INVOICE NOT_CONNECTED: scheduling and invoicing must be connected (or done by the owner) on day 1 so visits finish by day 14.

reviews.reasons: The re-plan responds correctly to the changed record. The projector-service card's directCosts is now $700 per visit (EVIDENCE) against the $650 signed price, so each deal loses $50 and the five orders would leave the owner $250 out of pocket once LumenTech is paid; Brain's ECONOMICS link fails and the opening is rightly excluded. The workbook is the remaining opening: 310 weekly-settling cinemas, 12% acceptance measured on this offer, Brain-produced spreadsheet (proved), $5 cost, card at checkout, 3 days to cash. Its $240 is a comparable-listing benchmark, so CONDITIONAL on a price test is the right stance, with the disagreement with Brain's OFFER_AND_PRICE recorded. Threshold check: 3 paid of 50 (6%) -> 3 + 0.06 x 260 = ~18 orders x $240 = $4,320 >= $3,000; at 12%, 14 orders need ~117 contacts. Stop (<3) and continue (>=3) cover every outcome; costs paid from settled receipts, no capital; last receipts settle about day 17 of 30.
findings: Recomputed: 14 x $240 = $3,360; cost $70; net $3,290; 117 of 310 contacts; settles by day 17 < 30.

Projector card is internally inconsistent: the fulfillment fact still reads 'written quote $300 per visit' while directCosts is $700. Treating the newer $700 directCosts as binding is the cautious reading; if the $300 quote still stood the five signed orders ($3,250) would be the better plan, so the owner should confirm which LumenTech cost is current.
Minor: the ledger's first receipts are day 6, after the day-5 test, so the test orders themselves are not shown; and s4 DELIVER (day 4) depends on s3 (day 6). Show the test-batch receipts by day 5.
Minor: dealsNeeded is marked EVIDENCED though it holds only if the price is $240.
Mailbox and checkout must be connected before day 1 (SEND_A_MESSAGE NOT_CONNECTED).
